annotatedSteps.description: Write balanced chemical equation for the electrolysis of brine
annotatedSteps.studentWork: NaCl + H₂O → NaOH + H₂ + Cl₂ (on passing electricity through brine)
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ½ Correct reactants and products identified, but the equation is not balanced as asked.

annotatedSteps.description: List two uses of one product (NaOH)
annotatedSteps.studentWork: NaOH is used for making soaps and detergents, and in paper making.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct; two appropriate uses of sodium hydroxide provided.

annotatedSteps.description: Identify compound A and compound B
annotatedSteps.studentWork: A is sodium hydrogen carbonate (baking soda), NaHCO₃. B is sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly identified both compounds A and B.

annotatedSteps.description: Chemical equation for heating compound A
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct and properly balanced thermal decomposition equation.

teacherNote: Marked against: (a) Balanced chemical equation for the electrolysis of brine (1); (b) Two valid uses of any one product (H₂ / Cl₂ / or NaOH) (1); (c)(i) Correct identification of A (NaHCO₃) and B (Na₂CO₃) (1); (c)(i) Balanced chemical equation for heating compound A (1). Well attempted! You accurately identified compounds A and B, gave valid uses of NaOH, and wrote the thermal decomposition equation correctly. Always ensure chemical equations are properly balanced when the question explicitly asks for a balanced equation.
